correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 48–73. Signed averaging preserves the range and its pointwise identity, hence reduces the global infimum to equivariant projections without changing the norm problem. In a mean-zero potential column, the endpoint transposition forces the signed coordinate difference and the opposite-coordinate stabilizer leaves exactly the two coefficients shown. The product decomposition then yields the three normalization equations: a complete-graph Laplacian is multiplication by its order on the mean-zero factor. These equations leave exactly one real parameter. I−Pᵀ, not generally I−P, bijects the cut and cycle projections. For 0≤t≤1 the pure-axis sum is 2(m−1)/m on the first orbit for both row and column: the absolute complete-graph difference mass is 2(m−1) and the other-coordinate weights are nonnegative with sum 1/m. The mixed block contributes 2(n−1)t/m to the column and 2(n−1)(1−t)/n to the row, since the row uses the opposite-axis input potential. The swapped contributions follow, and the cycle diagonals give the corrections 1−2d because 0<d<1. Each maximum has an interior crossing with opposite slopes and is convex on all of R (absolute sums), so the crossing is a global minimum, including against parameters outside [0,1]. The symbolic replay confirmed the four crossings, strict endpoint difference factors, and the four (3,4) values. The proof concerns the real unweighted edge coordinates, m≥3 and n>m, and does not require uniqueness of arbitrary minimizers.
residual_risks: The symbolic replay checks algebra, not the representation-theoretic reduction, which was checked separately. The frozen checker comment mentioning PQ=QP=0 is not an actual assertion and is not generally true for these adjoint-complement projections; the checker and theorem need only the separate idempotences.

value.rationale: Endpoint projection constants are intrinsic linear-extension/complementability invariants for natural graph subspaces. The product just beyond the equal-axis symmetry case separates l1 and l∞ in opposite directions for cut and cycle, and identifies the nonorthogonal optimizers. These exact values answer whether square-case endpoint equality survives unequal axes and give sharp benchmarks, rather than just bounds from a chosen projector.
residual_risks: No generalized optimality at intermediate p or on products with more factors is established.
